simple.meaning: עִדּוֹ (ʻIddôw) appears 11 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship and in connection with prophetic witness.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in 1 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah, and 1 more, beginning at 1 Kings 4:14. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family, family line, commandment, kingship, prophetic witness, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עִדּוֹ (H5714) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows עִדּוֹ through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: עִדּוֹ (ʻIddôw) / H5714 is tracked through 1 Kings 4:14, 1 Chronicles 6:6, 2 Chronicles 12:15, 2 Chronicles 13:22. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Ahinadab the son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;

timeline.evidenceText: Ahinadab the son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
Uzzi became the father of Zerahiah. Zerahiah became the father of Meraioth.

Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, aren’t they written in the histories of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, in the genealogies? There were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways, and his sayings are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
Now the prophets, Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and Jerusalem. They prophesied to them in the name of the God of Israel.

The elders of the Jews built and prospered, through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. They built and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.

definitions.short: Iddo (or Iddi), the name of five Israelites
definitions.full: H5714. Iddo עִדּוֺא עִדֹּא, עִדּוֺ, proper name, masculine Iddo ; — 1 father of an officer of Solomon עִדֹּא 1Kin 4:14 ; ᵐ5 Αχελ , A Σαδωκ , ᵐ5 L Αχιαβ 2 grandfather of prophet Zechariah עִדּוֺ Zech 1:1 , עִדּוֺא 1:7 ; ᵐ5 Αδδω . 3 a Levite עִדּוֺ 1Chr 6:6 ; ᵐ5 Αδει , ᵐ5 L Αδδω . 4 a priestly name עִדּוֺא van d. H. Ginsb (Baer עִדּוֺ ) Neh 12:4 ; א ᵐ5 etc. Αδαιας ; also עדיא 12:16 Kt ( עֲדָיָא ?), Qr עִדּוֺא ; א ᵐ5 τῷ Αδδαι , ᵐ5 L τῳ Αδαια . 5 a seer הַחֹזֶה עִדּוֺ 2Chr 12:15 = עִדּוֺ הַנָּכִיא 13:22 , ᵐ5 Αδ ( δ ) ω ; = יֶעְדּוֺ 9:29 , Ιωηλ ( δ ). עֹדֵד see עוד .
